prompt: Match each kind of record to the question it answers.
hint: The table at the top of the section.

pairs.right: which pairs talked, and how much

prompt: None of the three records holds the content of the conversation. Why is that deliberate?
hint: Compare how long each is kept.

choices.text: Content is encrypted, so there is nothing readable to store
choices.why: The lab's web traffic was plain HTTP; the reason is volume.

choices.text: Full capture lasts hours; these last months
choices.why: Right. Without the content they are small enough to keep.

choices.text: The firewall cannot see beyond the TCP header
choices.why: The sensor reads HTTP, DNS and TLS details, and records them.

choices.text: The law forbids keeping it
choices.why: The lesson's reason is size and time, not a prohibition.

prompt: Why does the administrator add the log rule at the end of the forward chain?
hint: Which packets reach the last rule?

choices.text: So that it logs every packet the firewall forwards
choices.why: Accepted packets stop at the rule that accepted them.

choices.text: Because nft appends to the end and cannot insert
choices.why: The feed rule is inserted at the top later on.

choices.text: It sees only what every rule above refused
choices.why: Right. Its log is the list of refusals.

choices.text: So that ulogd starts before the rule matches
choices.why: Position in the chain has nothing to do with ulogd.

prompt: How many seconds lie between start and end in each of remote's flow records?
A request took milliseconds, yet its flow record's end is two minutes after its start. What does that end mark?

choices.text: When the firewall forgot the connection
choices.why: Right. A closed TCP connection stays in the table for two minutes.

choices.text: When the shop sent its last byte
choices.why: That was milliseconds after the start.

choices.text: The moment ulogd was restarted by the administrator
choices.why: Both flows end 120 seconds after their own start.

choices.text: A clock that is two minutes wrong
choices.why: The same 120 seconds appears in both, from the same clock.

prompt: remote's three port probes appear in the drop log. Why are they missing from the flow records?
hint: Where do flow records come from?

choices.text: The flows were not yet written when the capture ran
choices.why: The script waited three minutes, enough for every entry.

choices.text: A dropped connection is never a confirmed table entry
choices.why: Right. No entry, no flow record.

choices.text: ulogd filters out flows on ports it does not know
choices.why: There is no such filter in the stack.

choices.text: Flows record UDP and the probes were TCP
choices.why: The flows shown are TCP to port 80.

prompt: Adding both directions, how many bytes did the flow that received the 404 page carry?
Somebody with root on fw empties drops.json. How many lines does admin's copy of drops.json hold right after?
hint: Lines were shipped as they were written.

choices.text: None, since rsyslog mirrors the truncation
choices.why: reopenOnTruncate only restarts reading from the top of fw's file.

choices.text: Four
choices.why: Right. The wipe on fw changes nothing on admin.

choices.text: Zero until rsyslog on admin is restarted, then four
choices.why: admin never lost them.

choices.text: Eight, because every line is sent again
choices.why: rsyslog remembers how far it has read.

prompt: From fw, port 514 on admin succeeds and port 22 times out. What does that arrangement give the defender?

choices.text: Faster delivery, since SSH no longer competes with the logs
choices.why: Bandwidth is not the point of the rule.

choices.text: Encryption of the lines on their way to the collector
choices.why: That needs TLS, which the lab does not use.

choices.text: An intruder on fw adds noise but leaves old lines as they were
choices.why: Right. The source cannot reach back into the collector.

choices.text: Proof that no line was lost in transit
choices.why: The disk queue helps with that, not the port rule.

prompt: Which of these make log shipping sturdier in production, as the section describes? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: TLS on port 514 with both certificates checked
choices.why: Right. It protects the lines in transit.

choices.text: A disk queue that retries while the collector is away
choices.why: Right. A restart on admin loses nothing.

choices.text: SSH from fw to admin, to repair the collection
choices.why: That is the reach back the design forbids.

choices.text: An alarm when a source goes quiet
choices.why: Right. Silence is a symptom of its own.

choices.text: Deleting each line on fw once it has been shipped
choices.why: The section keeps both copies; deletion is a retention decision.

prompt: A collector should raise its own alarm when a source goes ___ for longer than it ever has.
hint: It is either switched off or switched off by somebody.

prompt: Looking back through the collection, how many records came from 203.0.113.50?
A feed arrives naming three addresses. What does the section do with it first?

choices.text: Block the three at the top of the forward chain
choices.why: That is the second use.

choices.text: Send the addresses to the sensor as signatures
choices.why: The sensor is not involved.

choices.text: Search the stored flows and drops for them
choices.why: Right. Whether they already talked to us.

choices.text: Check that the publisher's certificate is valid
choices.why: The section judges a feed by its date and reason.

prompt: Why does the intel set carry timeout 1d?
hint: Who holds that address next month?

choices.text: nft sets need a timeout to accept elements
choices.why: The flag is a choice.

choices.text: It keeps the set small enough for the kernel
choices.why: Size is not the reason given.

choices.text: So attackers are blocked for a day and then forgiven
choices.why: A refreshed entry stays while the feed lists it.

choices.text: Addresses get reassigned, so a block expires with its reason
choices.why: Right. It falls out when the feed stops listing it.

prompt: Order remote's actions as the correlated timeline shows them, from first to last.
items: asked for /.env and raised the alert
trap: The port 23 attempt came three minutes after the rest.

prompt: The sensor's one alert was for /.env. What question does the timeline answer that the alert alone could not?
hint: Look at what the flows and drops add.

choices.text: Which signature matched
choices.why: The alert says that itself.

choices.text: Did anything else succeed?
choices.why: Right. Here only two page loads completed.

choices.text: What the /.env file contains on the server
choices.why: No record holds content.

choices.text: Which country the address belongs to
choices.why: Nothing in the three sources says that.

prompt: The sensor's clock runs three minutes slow and everything else is right. What happens to the merged timeline?
hint: Sorting by time is the whole join.

choices.text: The script refuses to sort mixed sources
choices.why: It sorts whatever it is given.

choices.text: Nothing, since the alert matches by address
choices.why: The address picks the records; time orders them.

choices.text: The alert lands before the page load it was about
choices.why: Right. Correlation needs every clock to agree, hence NTP.

choices.text: Flows shift three minutes, since they use seconds since 1970
choices.why: The flows come from fw, whose clock is right.

prompt: eve.json holds 43 records, 24 of them stats. What is the first saving the section names?

choices.text: Choosing which types of record are worth keeping
choices.why: Right. The stats records are most of the file.

choices.text: Keeping alerts for a shorter time
choices.why: Alerts are few and small; they are kept longest.

choices.text: Turning off compression to save processor time
choices.why: Compression is how space is saved.

choices.text: Moving the sensor's file onto fw
choices.why: That would undo shipping off the host.

prompt: Under the Marco Civil da Internet, how long must the lab's shop, an application on the internet, keep its access records?

choices.text: One year, like a connection provider
choices.why: That is article 13, for connection providers.

choices.text: Ninety days, as logrotate is set
choices.why: That is the lab's choice, not the law.

choices.text: For as long as the LGPD allows
choices.why: The LGPD limits; the Marco Civil sets a floor.

choices.text: Six months
choices.why: Right. Article 15.

prompt: Match each record to the starting retention the section proposes.
A feed published today names an address that, a report says, has been active since four months ago. Flows are kept 30 days. What can the look-back show?
hint: Retention decides how far back a question reaches.

choices.text: The whole four months, through the drop counts
choices.why: Counts per day carry no addresses.

choices.text: The last 30 days, and nothing of when it began
choices.why: Right. Why flows are kept 90 days to a year.

choices.text: Everything, if the IDS alerts are kept a year
choices.why: Alerts cover only what matched a signature.

choices.text: Four months, since the feed brings its own history
choices.why: A feed brings addresses and a reason, not your traffic.

prompt: The sensor alerts on one request from an address to /wp-admin. Which record tells you whether any other connection from it completed?

choices.text: The drop log
choices.why: It lists what was stopped, not what got through.

choices.text: The sensor's stats records
choices.why: Those describe the sensor itself.

choices.text: The flow records
choices.why: Right. Every allowed conversation has one.

choices.text: The threat feed
choices.why: It lists somebody else's observations.

prompt: At 03:00 the collector stops receiving anything from fw, whose logs had never paused for more than a minute. What does the lesson treat this as?

choices.text: A quiet night, since nothing was refused
choices.why: Flows keep coming whenever anything is allowed.

choices.text: A retention event, since logrotate runs at night
choices.why: Rotation renames files on admin; it does not stop fw.

choices.text: Harmless, because the disk queue will deliver it later
choices.why: The queue covers the collector's absence, not the source's.

choices.text: An alarm: fw is off, or somebody turned it off
choices.why: Right. Silence is checked for on its own.
